config.title: Component Library Theming

intro.title: Component Library Theming
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple themed component library by creating a set of reusable UI components—like buttons and cards—that share a consistent visual style. You will learn how to use React's Context API to manage and apply a theme (such as colors and fonts) across all components without manually passing props. The main technologies involved are React, JavaScript, and JSX for defining components and context. By the end, you'll understand how to centralize theme data and make your components dynamically adapt to different design systems.
intro.usecase: Component library theming is essential for maintaining consistent brand identity across large-scale applications like enterprise dashboards, e-commerce platforms, and SaaS products. Developers use theming to quickly switch between light/dark modes in productivity apps like Notion or Figma, or to apply custom brand colors to UI kits in design systems like Material-UI or Ant Design. This pattern allows teams to create reusable component libraries that adapt to different client branding requirements while maintaining a single codebase. Practical scenarios include building white-label applications where each customer needs their own color scheme, or creating accessible interfaces that support high-contrast themes for visually impaired users.

objectives: Initialize and apply a theme object to style a component library.
Configure a theme provider to distribute theme values across components.
Manipulate theme properties to update the visual appearance of components.
Integrate custom theme variables into component styling logic.
Bind component styles to dynamic theme values for consistency.
Construct a themed component that responds to theme changes.
Render a component library with a unified theme applied.

steps.title: Import React and createContext
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and createContext from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have access to React and the createContext API for building theme context.
successCriteria: React and createContext are imported from 'react'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React and createContext from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both React and createContext from 'react' using a single import statement.

steps.title: Create ThemeContext
steps.instruction: Create a ThemeContext using React.createContext() and assign it to a variable named ThemeContext.
steps.hint: Call React.createContext() and store the result in a const variable named ThemeContext.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a context for user data
const UserContext = React.createContext();
steps.expectedOutcome: A ThemeContext variable is created using React.createContext() and is ready to be used as a context provider.
successCriteria: ThemeContext is defined as a const variable using React.createContext().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using React.createContext() and assigning it to a const variable named ThemeContext.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ThemeContext wasn't created correctly. You need to call React.createContext() and store the result in a variable named ThemeContext.

steps.title: Create ThemeProvider component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ThemeProvider that accepts children as props and returns them wrapped in a ThemeContext.Provider.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called ThemeProvider that takes a children prop and returns <ThemeContext.Provider value={{}}>{children}</ThemeContext.Provider>.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ThemeProvider component is defined that will wrap children in a ThemeContext.Provider.
successCriteria: ThemeProvider is defined as a function component that accepts children and returns a ThemeContext.Provider wrapping those children.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure ThemeProvider accepts children as a prop and returns them wrapped in ThemeContext.Provider.
steps.feedbackWrong: ThemeProvider should be a function component that takes children and returns a ThemeContext.Provider wrapping them.

steps.title: Define theme objects
steps.instruction: Create two theme objects named 'lightTheme' and 'darkTheme' above the ThemeProvider component. Each should have a 'colors' property with at least 'background' and 'text' color values.
steps.hint: Define these as plain JavaScript objects with string color values. Place them before the ThemeProvider component so they're available to use.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two theme objects (lightTheme and darkTheme) are defined with color properties, ready to be used by the ThemeProvider.
successCriteria: lightTheme and darkTheme objects exist with 'colors' properties containing 'background' and 'text' color values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure both lightTheme and darkTheme objects have 'colors' properties with 'background' and 'text' values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The theme objects aren't defined correctly. Check that you have both lightTheme and darkTheme with color properties.

steps.title: Add useState to ThemeProvider
steps.instruction: Inside your ThemeProvider component, import useState from 'react' and use it to create a state variable called currentTheme that defaults to lightTheme.
steps.hint: Add the useState import at the top of your component, then call useState inside the component body with lightTheme as the initial value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemeProvider component will have a currentTheme state variable initialized with the lightTheme object.
successCriteria: useState is imported from 'react', and currentTheme state is initialized with lightTheme inside ThemeProvider.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've imported useState and initialized currentTheme with lightTheme.
steps.feedbackWrong: import useState and create a state variable called currentTheme that starts with lightTheme.

steps.title: Create toggleTheme function
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemeProvider component, create a function named toggleTheme that switches the current theme between lightTheme and darkTheme.
steps.hint: The toggleTheme function should check the current theme state and set the opposite theme.
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleTheme function is defined inside ThemeProvider that can switch between lightTheme and darkTheme.
successCriteria: The toggleTheme function is created inside ThemeProvider and correctly toggles between the two theme objects.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it properly toggles between lightTheme and darkTheme objects.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleTheme function is missing or doesn't correctly switch between the two theme objects.

steps.title: Return ThemeContext.Provider
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemeProvider component, update the ThemeContext.Provider's value prop to pass an object containing currentTheme and toggleTheme.
steps.hint: The value prop should be an object with two properties: currentTheme and toggleTheme.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemeContext.Provider will be ready to provide theme data and toggle function to child components.
successCriteria: ThemeContext.Provider's value prop contains an object with currentTheme and toggleTheme properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the value prop contains both currentTheme and toggleTheme properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ThemeContext.Provider needs to pass both the current theme and toggle function through its value prop.

steps.title: Create useTheme custom hook
steps.instruction: Create a custom hook named useTheme that calls useContext with ThemeContext and returns the context value.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses useContext to access the theme context and returns its value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A custom hook named useTheme is created that consumes the ThemeContext.
successCriteria: The useTheme function is defined, calls useContext with ThemeContext, and returns the context value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named useTheme, calls useContext with ThemeContext, and returns the context value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useTheme hook wasn't created correctly. It should be a function that uses useContext to access ThemeContext and returns the value.

steps.title: Wrap app with ThemeProvider
steps.instruction: Wrap the main App component with the ThemeProvider component in the render.
steps.hint: Place the App component inside the ThemeProvider tags to make the theme context available throughout your app.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is wrapped with ThemeProvider, making the theme context available to all child components.
successCriteria: ThemeProvider wraps the App component in the render.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure ThemeProvider directly wraps the App component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not wrapped with ThemeProvider. Check that ThemeProvider is placed as a parent of App.
